text:
Over 400 turns, the session closed the seven gaps in documents and finished with the gate not run, which it stated. Two problems cost it effort: a very large context and the lack of any byte or character counter.

**What the turns show**
- **Context size:** The context peaked at about 562k tokens, 304 turns ran above 200k, and about 412k tokens were consumed before the first write at turn 230. The costly early reads were the 52 KB capability list (turn 16, then re-read in part at turn 20), the 23 KB i170 review (turn 53) and the 18 KB i170 handoff (turn 57). The session also read six rule files and many specs in full before writing anything.
- **Size probes:** The session had no way to count bytes or characters, so it binary-searched spec sizes with `\A(?s:.){N}` greps. It probed sentence lengths with `.{N}$` greps in the same way.
  - Probing spans: turns 66-84, 224-227, 262-265, 273-279, 304-309 and 366-369.
  - Sentence-length probes: turns 167-173, 180-189, 200-201 and 238-243.
  - These made up a large share of the 99 search calls. A single character-count capability would have replaced them.
- **Unresolved placeholder:** The intent still contains `⟨missing:settings.conversation⟩`. The session never mentioned it, and I can't tell whether it mattered.
- **Scope:** All writes and edits went to the ADR, four specs and the hand-off under `docs/`, so the "documents only" rule held. The G7 finding said the spec needed no change and the fix was in code. The session still edited ISS-B14/AC13 (turns 282-287) to say where the pause reason comes from. That fits the "spec does not say which key supplies the reason" part of the finding, so I did not flag it.

The header lists no prompt sections, lessons, skills or subagent types, so the only conformance item is the "write documents only" instruction.
